propwash.guide.title: Flight school
propwash.guide.player.controls: Drag: rotate · Scroll: zoom · Double-click: reset view
propwash.guide.index.tip: Tip: hold %s over a Propwash item in any inventory to open its Flight school scene
propwash.guide.tab.intro: Short animated lessons about the workbench, the drone and flying. In any inventory, holding %s over a Propwash item opens the matching scene.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.title: Building a drone at the workbench
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.descrip: From parts to a ready-to-fly drone
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.be: Place a drone workbench and open it with a right-click. This is where you build a drone from parts – and take it apart again if needed.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.fr: The frame goes into the center slot, the stack (flight controller with ESCs) into the slot above it.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.mo: Fill all four motor slots and all four propeller slots on the arms – each set must be four identical parts.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.vi: The video unit at the nose decides the video system. The battery must fit the frame; it only charges in the battery charger.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.do: Once every slot holds a matching part, the finished drone appears in the result slot. It keeps the installed battery and its charge.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.pl: Place it and bind the remote
Right-click a block with the drone in your hand to place it. Then bind the remote by right-clicking the drone with it.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.fl: Right-click into the air with the bound remote to fly: FPV with matching goggles on, line of sight without goggles. Land first, then stop.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.callout: Drone workbench: top-down slots, 3D preview and flight stats
Frame – the backbone. It decides which parts fit.
Stack: flight controller with ESCs, stores the tune
Four identical motors on the arms
Four identical propellers on the motors
World rule “Parts must fit” off: then this pack fits too
Video unit: camera and transmitter, analog or digital
Empty batteries charge in the charger
Ready to fly! The drone waits in the result slot.
Bind the remote: right-click the drone with the remote in hand
Landed? Stop with the “Stop FPV flight” key or another right-click
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.st: The workbench shows weight without and with battery, thrust/weight, flight time and top speed. Red: doesn't fit. Yellow: flies, but has weaknesses.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.callout: Stats: weight without and with battery, thrust/weight, flight time, top speed
Red: error – the Li-Ion pack is too heavy for this frame
Yellow: warning – 4S fits, but the drone gets weak
propwash.guide.scene.bind.title: Binding the remote, wearing goggles
propwash.guide.scene.bind.description: Bind the remote – the goggles only have to match
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.remote.te: Hold the remote and right-click the placed drone. The remote remembers the drone, its receiver remembers you.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.remote: Remote in hand: click the drone
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.system: Digital goggles, digital drone: a match
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.wear.text: Goggles are not bound: just put them on – right-click into the air or use the head slot. The remote sees which goggles you wear.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.match.tex: When binding and starting, the remote checks your goggles: they must receive the drone's video. Wrong goggles: refused. No goggles: line of sight.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.mismat: Analog goggles, digital drone: the remote refuses
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.los: Goggles off: line of sight always works
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.keep.text: The receiver remembers you: workbench, pick-up, placing and restarts change nothing. A new flight controller needs a bind.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.keep: Workbench, pick up, place: the binding stays
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.takeov: If another pilot clicks it with their remote, it binds to them
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.start.tex: Right-click into the air with the bound remote. With matching goggles on you fly FPV, without goggles line of sight.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.fpv: Remote bound, matching goggles on: FPV
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.title: FPV and line-of-sight flight
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.description: Through the drone's camera or with your own eyes
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.step.fpv.te: With matching goggles on you see the drone's camera feed. Your body stays put with the remote in hand – and can still get hurt.
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.osd: In view: OSD with battery, signal, flight mode and time
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.step.los.te: Without goggles you fly line of sight with your own eyes. Your view turns smoothly and automatically towards the drone.
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.swi: Goggles off: continuing line of sight
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.fol: Your view follows the drone by itself
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.step.hud.te: Instead of the goggles OSD, a compact radio HUD shows battery, signal and flight mode. Walking and looking around are locked in flight.
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.hud: Remote HUD: battery, signal, flight mode
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.loc: Back to FPV: put matching goggles back on
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.step.stop.t: Land, then press the “Stop FPV flight” key or right-click with the remote again. The drone stays bound.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.title: Swapping and charging batteries
propwash.guide.scene.battery.description: Swap packs, check the fit and charge them
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.land.t: When the pack runs low, the OSD voltage sags on every punch and flashes – then land and disconnect. While armed or flown, the battery stays locked.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.menu.t: Sneak + right-click the drone to open its service menu: take the battery out or put a fitting one in; the four props sit next to it.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.non: Without a battery the drone can't be connected
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.swap.t: Faster with a fitting pack in hand: sneak + right-click inserts it directly and the old one goes to your inventory.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.cha: The drone takes the pack and its charge
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.fit.te: The frame decides which packs fit: cell count and maximum weight. The drone refuses a pack that is too heavy. The tooltip (Shift) shows what fits.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.fra: The frame carries at most 230 g of battery, this one weighs 420 g – the drone refuses it
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.rul: World rule “Parts must fit” off: then this pack fits too
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.che: Charges every pack: LiPo, LiHV and Li-Ion
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.charge: The charger charges every pack, Li-Ion too: up to four at once, about 1–3 minutes by size. Click it with a pack in hand to insert it.
propwash.guide.scene.race.title: Gates, courses and racing
propwash.guide.scene.race.description: Place gates, set a course, fly laps
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.place.tex: Hold a gate item and right-click the ground. The opening faces your view direction – that is the direction to fly through.
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.course.te: Click the gates in order with the course tool; the first one is start and finish. To take one out, use “Adjust gate”.
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.start.tex: Gate 1 pulses green while you are not racing. A start countdown can be switched on in the “Race” tab.
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.fly.title: Through the gates
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.fly.text: The next gate of your race glows green, all others white. Fly through them in the right direction and order.
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.next: After each gate, green moves on
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.lap.title: Lap and lap time
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.lap.text: Back through gate 1 after all gates: lap complete! Races have three laps by default. Leaderboard: /propwash race leaderboard
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.lap: Lap done: lap time, best lap, split
propwash.guide.scene.video.title: Video systems and goggles
propwash.guide.scene.video.description: Compare picture and latency of each video system
propwash.guide.scene.video.step.analog.t: Analog video has almost no delay. With distance and behind obstacles the picture gets noisier but stays usable for long.
propwash.guide.scene.video.callout.analo: Analog: about 12 ms latency, noisier with distance
Digital video gives a clear HD picture but a little more delay. At the edge of its range it stutters and freezes.
propwash.guide.scene.video.callout.digit: Digital: clear picture, about 26–30 ms latency
propwash.guide.scene.video.step.mismatch: Your goggles must receive the drone's video: analog to analog, digital to digital. With the wrong goggles the remote refuses and says why.
propwash.guide.scene.video.callout.misma: Analog goggles: can't receive digital video
propwash.guide.scene.video.step.creative: The creative goggles receive every video system. Set latency, range and noise in the configurator's “Video” tab.
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.title: Action cam: recording videos
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.descript: Real MP4 videos with motor sound from your FPV flights
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.mou: In the workbench the action cam goes into the “Accessory top” slot. The Light runs on the flight battery, the Heavy has its own and stabilizes.
Action cam on top of the frame
Light: 42 g, up to 1080p · Heavy: 150 g, stabilized, up to 1440p
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.rec: While flying FPV the “Record” key starts and stops the video. At the top right of the OSD, ● REC counts the recording time.
In the video: a clean image without OSD or interference
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.swi: In the “Modes” tab you put “Record” on the radio: a switch records while it is on, a button starts and stops with every press.
“Record” function on a switch or button
Record automatically when armed? Set it in the Action cam tab
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.lib: After stopping, the MP4 is saved in the background. In the configurator, “Browse recordings” lists every video with a thumbnail.
Action cam tab → Recordings: play, delete, open folder
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.fla: No video: the Action Cam (Flashback) records your FPV camera's path for the replay mod Flashback (Fabric only). Same button as above.
Action Cam (Flashback): needs the Flashback mod (Fabric)
In Flashback: one scene per flight to render, cut or change
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.title: Configurator: rates, PID, modes
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.descri: Understand sticks, rates, PID and flight modes
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.s: Right stick: pitch and roll, left stick: throttle and yaw (mode 2). Each stick movement turns the drone around one axis.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.r: Rates set how fast the drone turns: same stick input, faster rotation. Expo makes the center finer. Presets are in the “Rates” tab.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.p: The PID controller keeps the drone on the course your sticks command. Its values are derived automatically from the build.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.m: Angle levels the drone when you let go, Acro holds any angle for flips and rolls. Horizon mixes both.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.callou: Angle: let go – it levels out
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.s: In the “Modes” tab you put arming, flight mode, LEDs and more on radio switches. Every function also has a key – the last input counts.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.callou: Configurator only when landed and disarmed
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.title: Home point, return home, failsafe
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.description: GPS rescue brings the drone back safely
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.step.home.te: When first armed, the drone remembers its take-off spot as home point. A key sets it again at any time.
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.callout.home: Home point: this is where it returns
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.step.away.te: Lost your bearings behind trees or far out? The rescue key or a switch starts the flight home.
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.callout.resc: GPS rescue: fly home at a key press
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.step.failsaf: If the radio link drops, failsafe kicks in: by default the drone then flies home on its own.
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.callout.bloc: Walls and hills weaken the signal
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.callout.fail: Signal lost: failsafe starts the return
The drone climbs to a safe height, flies around obstacles to the home point, lands and disarms – even if you stop flying on the way.
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.callout.alon: Stop flying? It keeps going on its own
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.step.setting: Moving roll or pitch cancels the return and you take over. Set altitude, speed and failsafe in the “GPS rescue” tab.
propwash.guide.scene.rescue.callout.over: Move the sticks: you take over
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.title: Crashes, range and signal
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.descriptio: Flip back, fly on and find your drone again
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.crash: After a hard impact the flight controller cuts the motors (world rule “Disarm on crash”). Often the drone ends up on its back.
Once disarmed and still, “Flip drone upright” sets it back on its feet. Arming needs the throttle fully down and at most 25° of tilt.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.air.t: Disarmed mid-flight? With the max arm angle at 180° (configurator, “Configuration” tab) you can arm in any attitude – even in the air.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.ai: Disarmed: it falls and tips over
Arm angle 180°: armed again in the air
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.range: Full strength up to about 800 blocks, gone around 1200 (schematic). Creative, creative goggles or the Infinite range world rule: no limit.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.fu: Full strength up to about 800 blocks
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.walls: Depending on the video unit, the picture reaches about 250–520 blocks. Leaves weaken it a little, a trunk more, walls, hills and water a lot.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.wa: Solid blocks weaken the picture a lot
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.vi: Behind the pillar: picture gets noisy or freezes
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.beepe: Lost in tall grass? While connected and disarmed, the drone beeps with the locator beeper – just follow the sound.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.title: Swapping props and damage
propwash.guide.scene.repair.description: Crashes wear parts down – swap and repair props
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.crash.t: A prop shrugs off light bumps. Hard crashes damage every part: props first, motors much later, frame and electronics last.
A broken prop gives almost no thrust – the drone can't fly like this. Bent or cracked props cost thrust and add vibration to the picture.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.materia: PC bends and flies on, but worse; hard PC and glass-fiber nylon break into pieces; bi-blend sits in between. Carbon rarely breaks – then fully.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.bend: PC: bends, flies on but worse
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.crac: Hard PC, glass nylon: breaks into pieces
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.warning: The OSD warns you in flight, for example with PROP DMG, and the flight stats show crashes and condition. The drone tooltip lists every part.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.swap.ti: Swap props in the service menu
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.swap.te: Sneak + right-click opens the service menu, even with props in hand. Drop a prop on a slot to swap it; the old ones go to your inventory.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.swap: New props on, ready to fly
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.combine: Don't throw old props away: craft two damaged ones of the same kind together or put them in a grindstone – conditions add up, plus 5 %.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.pair: Two damaged props of the same kind
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.sum: Conditions add up plus 5 %, at most 100 %
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.bench.t: Motors, camera, frame, flight controller and battery are swapped at the workbench: take the drone apart, check the condition, replace the part.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.recy: Broken parts into the salvage slot: recycle
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.fly.tex: With fresh props the drone flies like new. Crash damage can only be switched off for the whole world: the Crash damage world rule.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.crea: Off only with the Crash damage world rule
propwash.guide.scene.survival.title: Survival: crafting parts
propwash.guide.scene.survival.descriptio: Craft parts and find them in chests
propwash.guide.scene.survival.step.craft: Every part is made at the normal crafting table – from iron, copper, redstone and other materials of the world.
The recipe book at a crafting table lists every part: search for “propwash” or its name. Every Propwash item explains itself with Shift.
propwash.guide.scene.survival.callout.no: Only creative goggles and creative FC: no recipe
propwash.guide.scene.survival.step.chest: Chests in structures around the world can hold Propwash parts too. Have a look before you craft everything yourself.
propwash.guide.scene.survival.callout.ch: With some luck: parts in chests
propwash.guide.scene.survival.step.works: Build the drone workbench and the charger first. A small whoop with a remote and analog goggles is a cheap way to start.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.w: Gravity, wind, battery and crash damage apply to all: World rules tab, presets and zones on top. The host and whoever may use /gamerule change them.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.callou: Applies to everyone in this world
Wind world rule: off to storm
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.menu: Service menu: props laid out like the drone
propwash.guide.scene.hold.title: Altitude and position hold
propwash.guide.scene.hold.description: ALTHOLD and POSHOLD: what they can do and where they fail
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.althold.t: A switch or the key turns on ALTHOLD: the drone levels itself and holds its altitude with the barometer.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.baro: The barometer measures air pressure – that gives the altitude
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.bobbin: Never quite still: it bobs about ±0.3–1 m
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.climb.tex: Throttle near the hold position keeps the altitude. More throttle climbs, less descends – both at a limited rate so it stays calm.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.climb: Throttle up: climbs slowly at the climb rate
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.poshold.t: With a GPS fix POSHOLD also holds the spot. Roll and pitch move the drone, releasing the sticks holds the new position.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.gps: GPS: accurate to 1–3 m, ten times per second
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.wind: Wind pushes it away, it creeps back slowly
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.no_gps.te: Under blocks, in caves, indoors or in deep ravines the receiver sees few satellites. Then POSHOLD does not work.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.roof: A roof above the drone hides the satellites
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.no_gps: OSD "NO GPS": only ALTHOLD left, it drifts
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.limits.te: Both modes help but are no autopilot: gusts, flying near the ground and speed disturb the sensors. Tune them in PID Tuning.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.never_: Never perfect: altitude ±1 m, position a few meters
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.tuning: PID Tuning: values for ALTHOLD and POSHOLD
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.stack.tex: Right-click a gate with a gate to put it on top – like a ladder with a shared middle bar. Each one stays its own course gate.
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.ladder: Ladder: zig-zag upwards – stack it while looking back to flip the gate
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.double: Double gate: top and bottom are separate course gates
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.mount.tex: Gates also go on walls and ceilings. Holding a gate, the Rotate gate key turns it; while sneaking it switches the mount, e.g. to a dive gate.
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.side: Side gate: one post on the wall, fly along the wall
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.dive: Dive gate: lies flat on the wall, fly through from above
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.hangin: Hangs from two straps under the ceiling
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.diving: Dive: the dive gate only counts downwards
propwash.guide.training.title: Flight training
propwash.guide.training.subtitle: %s lessons in %s chapters · %s/%s ★
propwash.guide.training.stars_time: ★★★ up to %s · ★★ up to %s · ★ within the %s time limit
propwash.guide.training.stars_distance: ★★★ up to %s m from the center · ★★ up to %s m · ★ anywhere on the pad
propwash.guide.training.how: How it works: put your drone down in an open spot, start flying with the remote and press “Fly”. The course appears as a hologram where the drone sits – only you see it and the world stays untouched.
propwash.guide.training.scale_note: Course for your drone: %s× the size, %s× the time
propwash.guide.training.tip: Tip: in flight, %s opens this window
propwash.guide.training.assisted_note: With flight aids (altitude/position hold, rescue, changed physics) you get one star at most.
propwash.guide.training.hud.waiting: Start flying with the remote to begin the lesson
propwash.guide.training.hud.land_first: Land and disarm – the course appears where the drone sits
propwash.guide.training.hud.blocked: No room for the course (%s blocks in the way) – fly to an open spot, land and disarm
propwash.guide.training.hud.no_ground: No ground for the landing pad – find a flatter spot
propwash.guide.training.hud.not_loaded: Terrain not loaded yet – wait a moment or raise the render distance
propwash.guide.training.hud.retry: Land and disarm to try again
propwash.guide.training.goal.heading: Turn the nose to pillar %s/%s
propwash.guide.training.goal.laps.start: Fly through gate 1 to start the lap
propwash.guide.training.goal.land: Land on the pad and disarm (%s m)
propwash.guide.training.event.missed: Missed ring %s – go back and fly through it!
propwash.guide.training.event.trick.outs: %s – outside the trick area, doesn't count
Rings, altitude, turns and the figure eight
propwash.guide.training.chapter.freestyl: Flip, roll, power loop, split-S and combo
propwash.guide.training.chapter.advanced: Dive gate, precision, low flight and the exam
propwash.guide.training.lesson.arm.title: Arming
propwash.guide.training.lesson.arm.descr: Arm, let the props spin for 2 s and disarm again.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.arm.tip: You can only arm with the throttle all the way down. Disarm only while the drone sits on the ground.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.hover.des: Climb into the box above the start pad and stay inside for 6 s.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.hover.tip: Raise the throttle slowly until the drone lifts off, then make small corrections. In Angle mode it levels itself.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.land.desc: Fly to the pad ahead, touch down gently and disarm.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.land.tip: Slow down before the pad (pitch back), then sink with a little less throttle. Stars depend on how close you land to the center.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.yaw.title: Yaw and orientation
propwash.guide.training.lesson.yaw.descr: Turn inside the box to face the four glowing pillars in turn.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.yaw.tip: Yaw only turns the nose. Hold your height with the throttle and stay inside the box.
Fly forward through five rings in a row.
Pitching forward tilts the drone – add a little throttle or it sinks.
Five rings at different heights: climb, sink, climb.
Throttle sets the height, tilt sets the speed. Start climbing early.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.turns.des: A wide right-hand turn through six rings.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.turns.tip: Clean turns combine roll and yaw: a little right roll, then follow with yaw.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.figure_ei: A figure eight around two pillars through seven rings.
Keep your height steady and look for the next ring before you pass the current one.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.gate_line: Six gates in a line as fast as you can – with split times.
Splits compare with your best run: green is faster, red is slower.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.slalom.de: Six offset gates in a zigzag.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.slalom.ti: Smooth lines beat sharp hooks: turn in early and take the gates at an angle.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.short_cou: Two laps of a loop with six gates.
Gate 1 starts the lap clock. The second lap compares every split with the first.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.flip.desc: Do a flip on the pitch axis inside the trick area.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.flip.tip: Above 5 m: cut the throttle, full pitch, then throttle up to catch it. Best in Acro mode.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.roll.desc: Do a roll on the roll axis inside the trick area.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.roll.tip: Like the flip, but with the roll stick. Level out straight after.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.power_loo: A full backwards loop under power.
Come in with speed, add throttle and pull back until you are upside down at the top, then keep pulling and catch it.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.split_s.d: Half roll upside down, then pull through downwards and fly back.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.split_s.t: Bring enough height: a split-S costs a few meters.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.combo.des: Three tricks back to back without a break.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.combo.tip: At most 3 s between tricks – flip, roll, flip is quickest.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.dive_gate: Climb over the flat gate and dive straight down through it.
Above the gate, nose down, almost no throttle, dive through and pull out early.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.precision: Six small rings in an S curve – every touch ends the attempt.
Slow is fast here: better clean than clipping a frame.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.low_fligh: Five flat rings just above the ground.
Little tilt and a soft throttle hand – ground effect lifts you slightly.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.final_exa: Two rings, a trick, a dive gate and a landing on the pad.
Everything from the chapters combined. Take enough height in the trick area.
propwash.guide.training.stars.distance3: up to %s m from the center
propwash.guide.training.stars.distance2: up to %s m from the center
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.title: Gripper: collecting items
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.description: Pick up items in flight, carry and drop them
In the workbench the gripper goes into the “Bottom accessory” slot, in place of the LED strip. It weighs 18 g and hangs under the nose.
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.cap: Up to 400 g in 4 stacks – never more than half the spare thrust
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.step.pickup: Arm and hover low over the items. Whatever lies under the drone goes into the gripper – as long as weight and stacks allow.
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.low: Hover low: below one block it grabs
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.hea: Cargo adds weight: more throttle, shorter flights
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.step.drop.t: Open it over the target: the “Cargo drop” key or a switch on the radio. The items fall with the drone's momentum, e.g. into a hopper.
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.swi: Or the “Drop cargo” switch in the Modes tab
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.step.auto.t: Landing and disarming sets everything down. In a hard crash the cargo falls out, nothing is lost.
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.lan: Disarmed on the ground: cargo set down
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.cra: Hard crash: the cargo falls out
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.title: Freestyle tricks
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.description: 50+ tricks: flips, loops, Matty, spins, Sbang and combos
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.step.flip_ro: In acro mode a full stick keeps the drone turning until you let go. One whole turn counts as a flip or a roll.
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.flip: Pitch stick all the way forward: flip
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.roll: Roll stick to the side: roll
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.step.juicy.t: Punch and flick forward into a half flip, then a half roll back upright. Afterwards you look back where you came from.
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.flic: Half flip forward until upside down
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.juic: Half roll back upright: Juicy Flick
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.step.rewind_: A rewind turns back the same way, as if the video ran backwards. The Rubik's Cube strings half flips and rolls together.
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.rewi: Half roll there and back: rewind
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.rubi: Half flip, full roll, half flip: Rubik's Cube
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.step.loops.t: Loop backwards over an obstacle with throttle, or turn around with a half roll downwards. A flip, roll or spin at the top makes a power flip & co.
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.powe: Throttle and pitch back: power loop over the wall
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.spli: Half roll, then pull through downwards: split-S
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.step.spins.t: Spin on the yaw axis while upside down: a full turn is an inverted yaw spin, while dropping it is a Trippy Spin.
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.inve: Half roll, then the yaw stick: inverted yaw spin
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.trip: Spin upside down while dropping: Trippy Spin
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.step.new_sch: Guillotines and Side Trippies use height and knife-edge, Sbang lives on ejects and quick reversals. 3D mode adds inverted flight and tic-tocs.
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.guil: Climb, dive straight down, flip out at the bottom: Guillotine
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.sban: An eject and two quick reversals: Sbang combo
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.step.combo.t: Land the next trick within 3 s and the combo grows up to ×4. Tricks flown straight into each other form a chain worth 25 % more.
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.chai: Flip straight into a roll: chain, +25 %
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.comb: Next trick within 3 s: combo up to ×4
propwash.guide.scene.tricks.callout.tab: “Freestyle” tab: 50+ tricks in nine families, with search and how to fly them
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.title: 3D mode
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.description: Reverse thrust: fly inverted, save loops, take off inverted
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.unlock: 3D is a flight mode of its own. Unlock it once in the configurator, then bind it to a switch or a key like angle mode.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.bin: Then bind it to a radio switch or a key
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.thrott: In 3D mode the throttle center means no thrust. Above it the props push up, below it the motors spin backwards and push down.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.cen: Center (1500 µs): no thrust, props at idle
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.up: Throttle up: forward thrust, the drone climbs
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.dow: Throttle down: motors spin backwards, thrust pushes down
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.wea: Normal props manage only about half the thrust in reverse
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.hov: Hover: throttle a little above center
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.invert: Upside down, throttle a little below center holds the height. 3D works with acro and horizon; angle always levels the drone upright.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.fli: Roll until inverted, throttle to the center meanwhile
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.hov: Inverted hover: throttle a little below center
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.con: Upside down, pitch and yaw feel reversed from your view
Reverse thrust to save a move
Full reverse thrust pushes down, faster than free fall. Save a move that came out too low or punch down before a bar.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.pun: Throttle all the way down: down faster than free fall
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.sav: Saves split-S and power loops that are too low
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.takeof: If the drone lies upside down, arm with the throttle centered and give reverse throttle: it takes off inverted, then roll it over.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.ups: Landed upside down? With 3D you don't need to flip it
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.arm: Arm only with the throttle centered
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.lif: Throttle down: reverse thrust lifts it off inverted
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.switch: Switch or key off: normal throttle applies at once. Altitude hold, GPS rescue and failsafe always fly without 3D.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.off: 3D off: throttle center now means half throttle, it climbs
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.res: Like angle mode to get out of trouble: flip the switch
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.rul: Servers can forbid 3D with a world rule
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.title: Rotating gates freely
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.descripti: Diagonal, tilted, as a diamond, any size and freeform gates
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.edit: Sneak + right-click a gate holding a gate or the course tool: the mouse wheel adjusts live, Enter applies. Hold Alt (Mac: Option) to use the mouse.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.angl: Yaw turns the gate like a compass, pitch tilts it, roll turns the opening within itself. The gate stays on its surface.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.size: Width and height of the opening go from 1 to 16 blocks in half steps. The item only sets the starting size.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.step: “Rotate gate” turns standing and hanging gates by the step set in the Racing tab: 90, 45, 15 or 5 degrees.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.free: No frame: right-click the edge of an opening and the blocks around it bound the gate. Caves, hallways and windows become course gates.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.callout.f: The blocks around it are the frame – the edge glows
Counts only inside the opening · at most 20 × 20 blocks (world rule)
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.des: Poles, turn flags and cubes for your course
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.ste: Set up the poles and append them in order with the course tool. When a pole follows a pole, the tool switches the side – your slalom.
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.cal: Arrows on the ground: pass here – the red cross is the wrong side
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.ste: Fly around the flag: past it, around behind it and back on the other side. The arrows on the ground show left or right around.
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.cal: Right around: the flag stays on your right
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.ste: Fly the cube like in MultiGP races: dive in from the top and out through the glowing side. You choose which side is the exit.
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.cal: In from the top, out through the glowing side
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.ste: The next element glows green like a gate. The HUD shows a wrong side or direction in red, and the element only counts once you fly it right.
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.cal: Around behind the flag and back
Climb, dive in, out the side
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.ste: Sneak + right-click with the element or the course tool: the mouse wheel sets heading, side or exit, height and scoring width, Enter applies.
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.cal: Side, height and scoring width with the mouse wheel
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.c: Under “Commands” in the “Modes” tab you put your own commands on switches or keys, like /time set night. They run as if typed, with your rights.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.arm.tip_m: Throttle keys or mouse wheel all the way down, then arm. The mouse only steers while you fly and no menu is open.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.hover.tip: Fine-tune the throttle with the mouse wheel. In Angle mode the mouse tilts the drone and it slowly levels out again – the middle mouse button levels it at once.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.yaw.tip_m: Yaw is on the side keys. Tap rather than hold – or pick “Mouse left/right: Yaw” in the Receiver tab.
Push the mouse forward a little and leave it there, the drone flies straight. Pull it back a bit to brake.
Pull the mouse back a little and leave it there, the drone flies straight. Push it forward a bit to brake.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.turns.tip: Move the mouse slightly sideways and tap the side key to yaw at the same time – small mouse movements are enough.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.flip.tip_: In Acro: cut the throttle and pull the mouse back briskly until the drone has gone around once, then stop the mouse and throttle up. The faster the mouse, the faster the flip.
In Acro: cut the throttle and push the mouse forward briskly until the drone has gone around once, then stop the mouse and throttle up. The faster the mouse, the faster the flip.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.roll.tip_: In Acro: swipe the mouse sideways briskly until the drone has turned once. When the mouse stops, the rotation stops.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.power_loo: Throttle up and pull the mouse back evenly until the loop is round. A large mouse pad helps.
Throttle up and push the mouse forward evenly until the loop is round. A large mouse pad helps.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.turtl: Turtle mode on (“Modes” tab), arm, push the stick toward the side to tip: those props spin backwards and flip the drone over.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.tu: Upside down: turtle mode on, arm
One side's props spin backwards and lift it over
Stays armed after crashes? World rule “Disarm on crash”
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.s: Left stick: pitch and yaw, right stick: throttle and roll (mode 1). Each stick movement turns the drone around one axis.
Left stick: pitch and roll, right stick: throttle and yaw (mode 3). Each stick movement turns the drone around one axis.
Left stick: throttle and roll, right stick: pitch and yaw (mode 4). Each stick movement turns the drone around one axis.
